requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is supplied, the collector unconditionally builds a contractless model and never inspects attributes on T. Consequently, a referenced type with [MessagePackObject], [Key], or [IgnoreMember] is serialized with ordinal string keys and all public read-write members instead of its declared MessagePack contract, violating the acceptance criterion that existing MessagePack attributes be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttributeHonouringReceiptTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured. It creates a referenced ProjectA type with [Key(0)] on Id and [IgnoreMember] on Secret, generates the formatter in ProjectB, and asserts integer-key/array output with Secret omitted. The current implementation instead selects CreateContractlessMembers, producing map output and including Secret.

findings.claim: A formatted type's own MessagePack attributes are ignored unless the caller duplicates its contract in a surrogate. In the no-surrogate path, the collector unconditionally builds members with CreateContractlessMembers. For example, a type with [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored gets a contractless string-key formatter that serializes Ignored, instead of the required [Key]/[IgnoreMember] behaviour.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129ReceiptTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursMessagePackAttributes. It generates a formatter for an attributed type and fails on head because generated source still contains the [IgnoreMember] property. A runtime companion can serialize the same object and show that Ignored is written and that string keys are used instead of the declared integer key.

findings.claim: The timestamp32 eligibility mask was inverted. nanoseconds shifted left by 34 always leaves the low 32 bits clear, so every positive-subsecond timestamp whose Unix seconds value is zero now takes the timestamp32 branch and loses its subsecond component. For example, 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z round-trips as 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z; a seconds value of 2^32 is likewise truncated by the 32-bit encoding.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129ReceiptTests.TimestampAtEpochWithSubsecondsRoundTrips. It serializes and deserializes 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z using MessagePackSerializer and fails on head because the result is the epoch without the 500 milliseconds. Also assert that an integral timestamp at Unix second 0 uses timestamp32 while a subsecond timestamp at that second uses timestamp64.

hunches.claim: The timestamp compact-encoding guard now tests the low 32 bits instead of the high 32 bits. An instant at the Unix epoch with nonzero subsecond nanoseconds therefore passes the timestamp32 path, which discards its nanoseconds; ordinary timestamps with nonzero seconds also lose the previous compact encoding. This changes the wire format and can corrupt deserialized values for existing users without any opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch.AddTicks(1) and DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch.AddSeconds(1) with base-built and head-built MessagePackPrimitives timestamp writing, compare the emitted bytes, and round-trip both values with the head build. The epoch-plus-one-tick case must expose the lost fractional value.

hunches.claim: When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always creates a contractless string-key member list and never reads attributes on T. Consequently [MessagePackObject]/[Key] contracts become name-keyed maps instead of integer-keyed arrays, and [IgnoreMember] members are serialized, contrary to the requirement that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate and use a formatter for T declared as [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)] public int A { get; set; } and [IgnoreMember] public int B { get; set; }, using A=1 and B=2. Compare its bytes with the established attributed formatter/standard resolver: the attributed contract is the one-element array [1], while this collector produces a string-keyed map containing A and B.

hunches.claim: When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds contractless string-key members and never reads attributes on T, so MessagePack attributes such as [Key] and [IgnoreMember] are ignored despite the acceptance criterion requiring them to be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test with a formatter declared without SurrogateType for a type marked [MessagePackObject], with Id marked [Key(0)] and another public writable member marked [IgnoreMember]. Serialize and assert a one-element integer-keyed array containing only Id, then round-trip it. The current contractless path instead emits a string-keyed map including the ignored member.

hunches.claim: The timestamp compactness mask is reversed: testing the low 32 bits for zero selects the 6-byte representation for values whose significant seconds are in the high 32 bits, truncating them during encoding.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a timestamp with Unix seconds 4294967296 and zero nanoseconds using base-built and head-built MessagePack code and compare bytes. Base uses the representation preserving 2^32 seconds; head takes bytesWritten = 6 with zero low bits, and deserializing the head bytes no longer produces the original timestamp.

hunches.claim: No test exercises the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are honoured. Every external data type is explicitly attribute-free, so the unconditional contractless collection path can ignore such attributes without any test failing.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test whose formatted type has [MessagePackObject] with non-sequential integer [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member, declare a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] without a surrogate, and assert the array shape, values, and excluded member. With the current unconditional CreateContractlessMembers call this should expose the missing behaviour.

hunches.claim: Surrogate tests use only integer keys. Consequently a formatter collector that always selects integer-key mode for surrogates would pass the entire added suite, leaving string-key surrogate output unverified.

hunches.claim: The contractless field writability check is not covered because ExternalPerson, ExternalPoint, and ExternalWidget contain only properties. A public read-only field could incorrectly enter the serialization model without a test failing.

hunches.claim: The explicitly supported body-less declaration form is never compiled by the tests: every annotated formatter has an opening and closing brace. A regression specific to semicolon-only partial class declarations would go unnoticed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
